quotes.verbatim_quote:
Here, the voice is cast into the role of
both storyteller and melodic/rhythmic
instrument. To achieve success in the
areas of story and rhythm, it is essen-
tial for the singer to develop a sense
of time and phrasing independent of
what the rhythm section lays down.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the foundational principle of the vocalizing chapter: the singer must internalize independent time rather than relying on the rhythm section.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
It is also vital for the vocalist, as it
is for any instrumentalist in this
music, to develop technical (scalar
and rhythmical) skills in order to mas-
ter the art of improvisation—to then be
free to explore nuance, possibility, and
depth.
quotes.why_load_bearing: States the method's core pedagogical sequence: technical mastery of scales and rhythm is the prerequisite that unlocks expressive freedom.

quotes.topic: E diminished chord, Y.M.B. in S.
quotes.verbatim_quote:
Demonstrated in the following four figures are examples of the last
2 bars of “Y.M.B. in S,,” incorporating notes of the diminished chord.
Examples are notated in the keys of F and C minor. C7 (in the key of F
minor) uses the E-diminished chord; while G7 (in the key of C minor)
uses the B diminished chord.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Establishes the key-specific rule for choosing the related diminished chord: C7 in F minor → E-diminished, G7 in C minor → B-diminished.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
An Ab augmented arpeggio (the 5th degree is raised a half-step from
the major)
quotes.why_load_bearing: Gives a precise, in-text definition of the augmented arpeggio as a variant of the major arpeggio with the 5th raised a half-step.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
The Ab whole tone scale (a six note scale built on whole-steps
above the root)
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the whole tone scale concisely within the warm-up series, establishing its structure as a six-note, all-whole-step construction for use in improvisation.
